title: LLM-Based Invariant Testing for Software Functional Bugs
datasets: Lisa-Bench: 7 open-source C/C++ libraries for coverage/API-sequence evaluation
Historical functional bug set: 25 developer-fixed bugs across five libraries
TECO-derived oracle-completion prefixes: 500 cases, mutation-valid N=362
task: Generate C/C++ API-sequence unit tests with documentation-grounded invariants; detect silent functional bugs in libraries. Evaluation also includes branch/line coverage and historical bug reintroduction.
input_setting: Public API metadata/docs and generated straight-line API call sequences; API sequence stage uses nn-gram feedback, invariant stage segments sequences and inserts semantic assertions, verifies each on reference build, then tests on buggy historical build.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper Data Availability links Zenodo reference [66] and both GitHub repositories. Zenodo title/creators match paper; archive contains DCAware source, results, prompts and data. CNTG README describes invariant-generation component; CGNTG README identifies PromptFuzz API-sequence/fuzz-driver predecessor.
source_commit_or_archive: Zenodo 21357436 (latest version of concept DOI 19238006); archive MD5 listed by Zenodo 2fbe9471653b1e5093e317ab3db3c619; GitHub CNTG HEAD 1d757ad7081cfd556079a1b24827059b902ab379; CGNTG HEAD afa7e8e9c5a871eec9cb3eff6fd604a16704cf97.
license: DCAware source archive contains MIT LICENSE; Zenodo record CC BY 4.0. Component GitHub repos do not declare licenses, but full implementation is included under Zenodo archive MIT license.
exact_models: Main paper comparison: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 via vLLM and GPT-5-mini via Azure API.
DCAware source defaults Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8, temperature 0.2; artifact setup reports one A100 40GB.
weights_status: Qwen3-Coder weights are open but not bundled; vLLM on 40GB A100 required. GPT-5-mini is hosted Azure. No fine-tuning reported.
evaluation_route: Author Zenodo ZIP manifest was inspected via HTTP Range without full download or extraction: 18,134 entries/1.69GB expanded, 32 Python files, source, data, prompts, supplementary paper, Docker oracle runner and saved results. Cached DCAware outputs contain 500 result files for each primary model; ChatAssert 494 each. Public README includes smoke checks, run/evaluation/PIT scripts and Java 8/21/Maven/Docker environment. No code execution or model/API calls.
blockers: Setting is oracle completion with a provided test prefix and current code treated as expected behavior; it does not generate issue-reproduction tests from buggy/fixed Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT instances.

Full rerun needs C/C++ toolchains, Java 8 and 21, Maven, Docker, PIT mutation testing, Qwen3-Coder-30B on a 40GB A100 or Azure GPT-5-mini. Cached results allow offline analysis; paper reports $0.87 total GPT-5-mini cost for 500 cases.
Oracle validity is not formally proven; candidates are high-confidence bug reports that developers must confirm. Documentation coverage bounds recall.
Lisa-Bench historical set is only 25 bugs (five each in five libraries) and reported main table is one representative run; authors show three-run stability on three libraries.
The ZIP is large (1.26GB compressed); it was manifest-inspected by range but not fully downloaded/executed.
concept_fit: Very high for oracle/concept reasoning: invariants encode structural, range, relational/conservation and documentation-derived semantic contracts, placed at chunk boundaries; runtime state queries target assertion intent. Strong related work on separating execution success from fault-revealing strength.
recommendation: Prioritize for oracle-quality theory and artifact analysis. The full public artifact is unusually complete and includes all main outputs and a reproducibility smoke path. Use as an oracle-quality baseline, not as a historical issue-reproduction generator: the task assumes test prefixes and current code is the reference. Exact full rerun is conditional on Java/PIT/Docker and GPU/Azure setup.
